summary.text: Keith Mogel is the Democratic candidate for the Wisconsin State Assembly, District 75, in the November 3, 2026 general election, facing incumbent Republican Duke Tucker. A retired Army National Guard lieutenant colonel and operations manager, he lists rural school funding, rural health care and rural infrastructure as his main campaign messages.

paragraphs.text: Keith Mogel graduated from Emmaus High School, earned a bachelor's degree from Pennsylvania State University in 1977 and a graduate degree from the University of Wisconsin-Eau Claire in 1989, and served in the U.S. Army National Guard from 1977 to 2005, according to Ballotpedia.

In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he attended Penn State on an ROTC scholarship, was commissioned as a second lieutenant, served 11 years on active duty and 17 years in the Wisconsin and Minnesota National Guard, and retired as a lieutenant colonel.
He said he has since worked for small and large businesses, earned a Six Sigma black belt and taught production and inventory control certification courses.
Mogel advanced from the Democratic primary on August 11, 2026.

In the survey he said he wants to overhaul school funding and restructure the school voucher program, create a state-managed small business insurance cooperative and expand BadgerCare to allow single-payer purchase by self-employed people, and overhaul the state road funding formula for rural towns and counties.
He also named funding for the Department of Natural Resources and state parks among his personal priorities.
